news.title: Virgil van Dijk hits back at ‘nonsense’ claims that he influenced Netherlands’ World Cup tactics
news.lede: Virgil van Dijk has strongly rejected accusations that he dictated former head coach Ronald Koeman’s tactical setup during the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign, branding the allegations "completely baseless". Addressing Dutch reporters in a tense press conference, the Liverpool captain and national team skipper called suggestions that he drove tactical changes prior to their last-16 elimination by Morocco "utter nonsense". Directing his response to a journalist, Van Dijk said: "One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. He added: "The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup; those are the hard facts.

news.title: Harri Stevens: Swansea Kicks player to Street Child World Cup
news.lede: Harri Stevens used to lose his temper on a football pitch. At 12, in a clip Swansea City AFC Foundation has just put out, he says it himself: “Before I started going Kicks, I was like naughty when I was out. But since I’ve gone there, like, I’ve just been behaving.” This spring, at 16, he walked out in a Wales shirt at the Street Child World Cup in Mexico City.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: 1,000-goal target and Portugal ambition fuel football icon
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo made his Portugal debut in 2003 and is set to win his 234th cap against Wales. Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring after the World Cup but says he opted to extend his glittering career as he believes he can help Portugal to further success - and reach a personal milestone of 1,000 career goals. The 41-year-old confirmed in the summer that the 2026 World Cup would be his last, although his long-term future remained uncertain. However, he has been included in Jorge Jesus' 25-man squad for Portugal's Nations League campaign, which begins against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night.

news.title: England players carrying 'scar' from World Cup exit, says Bukayo Saka
news.lede: Bukayo Saka started three of England's eight games at the World Cup. England winger Bukayo Saka says the team are still carrying the "scar" of their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina. Thomas Tuchel's team were on the verge of becoming the first England side to reach a men's World Cup final since 1966, but were stunned by two late Argentina goals as they fell to a 2-1 loss. A thrilling 6-4 victory over France in the bronze medal match gave the Three Lions their best World Cup finish in six decades, but the wait for their second trophy goes on.

news.title: FOOTBALL - World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit sees 'no strong reason' for Coventry City boss Frank Lampard to become next England manager
news.lede: And Petit also won 63 caps for France and lifted the World Cup and European Championships on the international stage. He scored the third goal in the 1998 FIFA World Cup final as France thrashed Brazil 3-0 on home soil in Paris. Petit played alongside Coventry boss Lampard for just over two seasons at Chelsea. Tuchel has not yet convinced Petit he is the right manager to lead England.
